For example, a reviewer can decline head A in a review whose `commitOid` is A, the PR can move to head B, and this check will accept that still-listed review as proof that the leg is unavailable for B; the resulting terminal report then incorrectly labels B as `targetSnapshotHead`. Require target-scoped evidence to carry and match the final HEAD (or otherwise establish explicit current-head provenance) rather than only being present in the final fetch. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎. - src/collector-receipt.ts:490: **![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat) Reject cross-leg evidence on valid classifications** With multiple configured legs, a `valid` candidate can include its own qualifying review plus arbitrary evidence from another leg. This loop stops after finding one qualifying record and never validates the remaining refs, yet all of them are retained in that leg's `evidenceRefs` and embedded in the receipt. A model response such as leg A citing both A's and B's reviews therefore corrupts the per-leg provenance consumed downstream; validate ownership of every supplied ref or normalize the list to approved proof before retaining it. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎. - src/collector-receipt.ts:647: **![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat) Reject missing when a qualifying review is present** At or after the cutoff, this branch accepts `missing` without checking whether the final snapshot already contains an expected-author, exact-HEAD, before/within review that satisfies `reviewQualifiesForValid`. The model can cite only the final snapshot—or even cite that qualifying review, since `missingCiteAllowed` permits expected-author reviews—and the runtime will emit a false `missing` terminal status instead of `valid`. Scan the final snapshot with the shared qualification predicate and reject `missing` whenever valid completion evidence exists. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎. - src/collector-evidence.ts:370: **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Preserve uncertainty when re-observing edited reviews** When an edited review version is first observed, this code correctly sets its `authoritativeTime` to `null`; on a later unchanged observation, however, `isNewVersion` is false and no branch restores that historical `null`, so the freshly normalized pending record keeps the original `submittedAt`. `buildObserveModelView` exposes that pending copy as before/within even though `storeEvidence` retains the same evidence ID as uncertain, causing the model to see eligible proof that receipt validation subsequently rejects. Reuse the stored version's authoritative timestamp whenever a review version has already been seen. Useful? React with 👍 / 👎. - src/collector-receipt.ts:654: **![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat) Embed evidence referenced by included snapshots** An included snapshot retains its complete `evidenceIds` array, but this loop embeds only the final snapshot's pull-request and authenticated-user records; later filters add configured-author and request-marker records while still omitting unrelated comments and reviews. raw.title: feat: add standalone Collector v1 role
raw.body:
## Summary

Add a standalone, caller-independent `collector` role for external GitHub PR review collection.

Collector v1:

- requires explicit `github.com` repository, PR number, and versioned non-empty reviewer-leg manifest;
- has no default or guessed bot;
- uses purpose-built observe/request/wait/output tools rather than unrestricted mutation tools;
- owns a 15-minute controlled collection cutoff with early terminal completion;
- binds completion to a complete timestamped final PR snapshot;
- preserves all prior-head review findings with tagged provenance;
- distinguishes current `valid | unavailable | missing` leg outcomes;
- preserves immutable paginated evidence in a self-contained receipt;
- fails loudly on malformed configuration, transport failure, incomplete pagination, evidence overflow, and repeated PR identity drift;
- categorically forbids every Skill and documents the supported isolated launch profile;
- contains no orchestration, routing, merge, Judge, Fixer, or next-role behavior.

## Review closure

Constructed through Coder → Judge → Reviewer → Judge → Fixer closures with forward-only commits. The fresh full-range Reviewer found a repeated-drift atomicity defect; the final repair now fails closed before evidence/snapshot certification when the one allowed retry also drifts. Judge converged Collector v1 at `a817975`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`
- initially empty-HOME full suite: 197/197
- `npm pack --dry-run`: 26 packaged files, no copied canonical Skill
- `git diff --check`
- clean worktree

## Commit range

`c5f75b6...a817975`

## Dependency

Stacked on the role-runtime architecture PR. Merge that base PR first.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Large new role with external GitHub mutation (issue comments), complex eligibility/cutoff and receipt validation, and reliance on ambient `gh` auth—fail-closed paths are extensive but misconfiguration or transport edge cases could still affect collection outcomes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds the **Collector** workflow role: a one-shot Pi role that observes configured external GitHub PR review legs on `github.com`, optionally posts correlated request comments, waits within a **15-minute eligibility window**, and terminates with a self-contained **`ak_collector_output`** receipt (`valid` / `unavailable` / `missing` per leg—not `refused`).
> 
> **Surface and wiring:** `--ak-role collector` with `--ak-collector-repo`, `--ak-collector-pr`, and `--ak-collector-legs` (v1 JSON schema + packaged `schemas/collector-legs-v1.schema.json`). Role runtime and package extension load collector soul, `gh`-backed transport, and gate to four tools only; Skills and ambient instruction surfaces are forbidden on the supported isolated launch profile.
> 
> **Runtime core:** Manifest/repo parsing with fail-closed validation; ledger with strict assistant-batch rules (one operational or one output call); observe with pagination, 8 MiB snapshot / 32 MiB receipt caps, PR bracket retry on HEAD drift; process-local at-most-once requests with HTML markers and ambiguous-loss recovery via observe; receipt builder that embeds full `snapshots[]` and `evidenceRecords[]` with ref resolution and cutoff/missing laws.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c73bf31a3d22815b26b9a33a5d28fd1f242f5701. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

performed_via_github_app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind target-scoped unavailability to the target HEAD**

When the PR HEAD changes, GitHub continues returning reviews and comments made against the previous HEAD, so mere membership in the final snapshot does not make evidence target-scoped. For example, a reviewer can decline head A in a review whose `commitOid` is A, the PR can move to head B, and this check will accept that still-listed review as proof that the leg is unavailable for B; the resulting terminal report then incorrectly labels B as `targetSnapshotHead`. Require target-scoped evidence to carry and match the final HEAD (or otherwise establish explicit current-head provenance) rather than only being present in the final fetch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject cross-leg evidence on valid classifications**

With multiple configured legs, a `valid` candidate can include its own qualifying review plus arbitrary evidence from another leg. This loop stops after finding one qualifying record and never validates the remaining refs, yet all of them are retained in that leg's `evidenceRefs` and embedded in the receipt. A model response such as leg A citing both A's and B's reviews therefore corrupts the per-leg provenance consumed downstream; validate ownership of every supplied ref or normalize the list to approved proof before retaining it.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve uncertainty when re-observing edited reviews**

When an edited review version is first observed, this code correctly sets its `authoritativeTime` to `null`; on a later unchanged observation, however, `isNewVersion` is false and no branch restores that historical `null`, so the freshly normalized pending record keeps the original `submittedAt`. `buildObserveModelView` exposes that pending copy as before/within even though `storeEvidence` retains the same evidence ID as uncertain, causing the model to see eligible proof that receipt validation subsequently rejects. Reuse the stored version's authoritative timestamp whenever a review version has already been seen.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Embed evidence referenced by included snapshots**

If GitHub returns a 2xx response after creating the request comment but its body is truncated, malformed, or missing a field required by `normalizeIssueComment`, the exception from this success branch falls into the generic catch and is reported as `rejected`. The ledger then fatally terminates instead of recording an ambiguous response loss that a subsequent observation could recover via the deterministic marker, so a caller retry can post a duplicate even though the first request succeeded.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve author provenance for inline-comment replies**

When another GitHub account replies to an inline review comment, the reply can carry the same `pull_request_review_id` as the configured author's review, so this predicate joins it into that leg's review report without checking `record.authorLogin`. Because `reviewInlineText` then renders only location and body, downstream consumers see the reply as though it were authored by the reviewer leg; either restrict review-owned inline evidence to the review author or render reply authorship explicitly.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match the published request-body schema to runtime validation**

A manifest request body containing only whitespace or more than 60,000 UTF-8 bytes validates against this advertised machine-readable schema because it specifies only `minLength: 1`, but `loadCollectorManifest` rejects the same document at startup. Callers therefore cannot use the packaged schema to determine whether a manifest is accepted; expose the nonblank and size constraints in the published contract, using an explicit byte-limit annotation or equivalent validation metadata where standard character-count keywords are insufficient.

## Summary

Add a standalone, caller-independent `collector` role for external GitHub PR review collection.

Collector v1:

- requires explicit `github.com` repository, PR number, and versioned non-empty reviewer-leg manifest;
- has no default or guessed bot;
- uses purpose-built observe/request/wait/output tools rather than unrestricted mutation tools;
- owns a 15-minute controlled collection cutoff with early terminal completion;
- binds completion to a complete timestamped final PR snapshot;
- preserves all prior-head review findings with tagged provenance;
- distinguishes current `valid | unavailable | missing` leg outcomes;
- preserves immutable paginated evidence in a self-contained receipt;
- fails loudly on malformed configuration, transport failure, incomplete pagination, evidence overflow, and repeated PR identity drift;
- categorically forbids every Skill and documents the supported isolated launch profile;
- contains no orchestration, routing, merge, Judge, Fixer, or next-role behavior.

## Review closure

Constructed through Coder → Judge → Reviewer → Judge → Fixer closures with forward-only commits. The fresh full-range Reviewer found a repeated-drift atomicity defect; the final repair now fails closed before evidence/snapshot certification when the one allowed retry also drifts. Judge converged Collector v1 at `a817975`.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`
- initially empty-HOME full suite: 197/197
- `npm pack --dry-run`: 26 packaged files, no copied canonical Skill
- `git diff --check`
- clean worktree

## Commit range

`c5f75b6...a817975`

## Dependency

Stacked on the role-runtime architecture PR. Merge that base PR first.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Large new role with external GitHub mutation (issue comments), complex eligibility/cutoff and receipt validation, and reliance on ambient `gh` auth—fail-closed paths are extensive but misconfiguration or transport edge cases could still affect collection outcomes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds the **Collector** workflow role: a one-shot Pi role that observes configured external GitHub PR review legs on `github.com`, optionally posts correlated request comments, waits within a **15-minute eligibility window**, and terminates with a self-contained **`ak_collector_output`** receipt (`valid` / `unavailable` / `missing` per leg—not `refused`).
> 
> **Surface and wiring:** `--ak-role collector` with `--ak-collector-repo`, `--ak-collector-pr`, and `--ak-collector-legs` (v1 JSON schema + packaged `schemas/collector-legs-v1.schema.json`). Role runtime and package extension load collector soul, `gh`-backed transport, and gate to four tools only; Skills and ambient instruction surfaces are forbidden on the supported isolated launch profile.
> 
> **Runtime core:** Manifest/repo parsing with fail-closed validation; ledger with strict assistant-batch rules (one operational or one output call); observe with pagination, 8 MiB snapshot / 32 MiB receipt caps, PR bracket retry on HEAD drift; process-local at-most-once requests with HTML markers and ambiguous-loss recovery via observe; receipt builder that embeds full `snapshots[]` and `evidenceRecords[]` with ref resolution and cutoff/missing laws.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c73bf31a3d22815b26b9a33a5d28fd1f242f5701. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
